article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

tasks.prompt: What is the central development reported in the article?
options: The House of Lords approved an assisted-dying law
The government made assisted dying a party-policy issue
MPs rejected a new assisted-dying bill, ending this attempt to change the law
The courts ordered Parliament to hold another vote
tasks.correct_answer: MPs rejected a new assisted-dying bill, ending this attempt to change the law
tasks.explanation_hebrew: בית הנבחרים דחה את הצעת החוק, ולכן הניסיון הנוכחי לשנות את החוק באנגליה ובוויילס הסתיים.

tasks.prompt: What was the result of the House of Commons vote?
options: 270 to 286 in favour
286 to 270 against, a majority of 16
300 to 256 against, a majority of 44
A tie that was decided by the Speaker
tasks.explanation_hebrew: 286 חברי פרלמנט הצביעו נגד ו־270 בעד, ולכן ההצעה נפלה ברוב של 16.

tasks.prompt: What does “free vote” mean in this parliamentary debate?
options: The public could vote without registering
MPs voted without attending the Commons
The vote had no legal consequences
MPs were not required to follow party lines
tasks.correct_answer: MPs were not required to follow party lines
tasks.explanation_hebrew: free vote הוא הצבעה שבה חברי הפרלמנט רשאים להצביע לפי שיקול דעתם ולא לפי משמעת מפלגתית.

tasks.prompt: Which safeguards were included in the proposed bill?
options: Approval by two doctors and an expert panel
Approval by one relative and a local councillor
A nationwide referendum for every application
Automatic approval after a six-month wait
tasks.correct_answer: Approval by two doctors and an expert panel
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הצעת החוק דרשה אישור של שני רופאים ושל פאנל מומחים לבקשה לסיוע במוות.

tasks.prompt: Why does the article suggest the issue is likely to return to Parliament?
options: The vote automatically requires a second reading next week
The House of Lords can enact the rejected bill alone
Supporters and senior figures say another proposal may be introduced in a future session
The prime minister ordered MPs to reverse their votes
tasks.correct_answer: Supporters and senior figures say another proposal may be introduced in a future session
tasks.explanation_hebrew: למרות הדחייה, תומכים ובהם קים לידביטר ולורד בלנקט אמרו שהסוגיה לא נעלמת ושייתכן ניסיון נוסף כבר בשנה הבאה.

tasks.prompt: What does “coerced” mean in critics' warning about vulnerable people?
options: Given additional medical care
Protected by a panel
Allowed to change their minds
Pressured or forced into a decision
tasks.correct_answer: Pressured or forced into a decision
tasks.explanation_hebrew: coerced פירושו להיות נתון ללחץ או כפייה; המתנגדים חששו שאנשים פגיעים יידחפו לסיים את חייהם.

tasks.prompt: Compare the parliamentary progress of the previous bill with Lauren Edwards's new proposal.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להשוות בין האישור הקודם בבית הנבחרים, העיכוב בבית הלורדים, הניסיון המחודש והדחייה הנוכחית.
expected_points: Kim Leadbeater's earlier bill passed the Commons on 20 June 2025
It passed with a majority of 23
It stalled and ran out of time in the House of Lords
Peers had tabled more than 1,200 amendments
Lauren Edwards reintroduced proposals so peers could finish scrutiny
The new bill was rejected at its second reading
The 2026 vote was 286 to 270 against
The current bill will make no further progress

tasks.prompt: Explain the main ethical and practical disagreement between supporters and opponents described in the article.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג באופן מאוזן את טיעוני הבחירה והסבל מול חששות הכפייה, הבטיחות והעדיפות לטיפול פליאטיבי.
expected_points: Supporters argue terminally ill adults should have choice and control
They say some suffering cannot be relieved by palliative care
They argue the existing law leaves people without safeguards
Opponents fear vulnerable people could be coerced
Critics say the bill's safeguards were insufficient
Medical and professional bodies were said not to attest to its safety or workability
Opponents prioritise improving NHS, social and palliative care
Some fear legalisation would alter the doctor-patient relationship

tasks.prompt: Summarise the bill, the vote and the principal arguments on both sides.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לסכם באנגלית את תנאי הזכאות וההגנות, תוצאת ההצבעה, טיעוני שני המחנות ומה צפוי בהמשך.
expected_points: The bill covered terminally ill adults expected to live fewer than six months
Applicants would need approval from two doctors and an expert panel
MPs had a free vote
The Commons rejected the bill 286 to 270
Supporters emphasised autonomy and relief from suffering
Opponents emphasised coercion risks and inadequate safeguards
Some opponents called for better palliative care first
This attempt is over in the short term
Supporters may introduce another bill in a future session

tasks.prompt: Write a neutral parliamentary briefing explaining the vote and why the debate remains unresolved.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכתוב באנגלית תדריך עובדתי ומאוזן, ללא נקיטת עמדה, הכולל את ההצעה, ההצבעה, ההגנות, הביקורת והאפשרות לניסיון נוסף.
expected_points: Identify the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill
State the eligibility threshold of fewer than six months to live
Describe the two-doctor and expert-panel safeguards
Report the 286-to-270 rejection and majority of 16
Explain that MPs had a free vote
Present supporters' arguments fairly
Present opponents' arguments fairly
Clarify that the proposal will not progress now
Note that future legislation remains possible
Maintain neutral language throughout
